items.prompt: White to move on move 5. Black's knight attacks e4. Find a sound move.

claims.statement: Castling, d3 and Nc3 are each within 40 cp of the engine's top choice (depth 16).
5.Nxe5 scores at least 200 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Which piece of White has not moved at all and could use a safer home?
The pawn on e4 can be defended or left for a moment; the king can go to safety.
Castle (O-O); 5.d3 and 5.Nc3 also work.
items.explain: Castling brings the king to safety and the rook into play, and 5.d3 or 5.Nc3 defend the pawn on e4 directly. Capturing on e5 would trade a knight for a pawn. At depth 16 castling, d3 and Nc3 are each within 40 cp of the best move.

feedback_by_move.f3e5: The knight takes a pawn and is taken back; White has given a knight for a pawn and the engine rates this far worse.

items.prompt: White to move. Black castled, White took on c6 and Black retook with the d-pawn. Does 1.Nxe5 win a pawn?

claims.statement: Nxe5 wins at least a pawn along the engine's line.
No black piece defends the pawn on e5.
The rook on e1 defends e4, so the queen cannot take it.

hints: Count the defenders of e5.
The knight that defended e5 is gone, and the rook stands behind e4.
Yes: Nxe5 wins a pawn.
items.explain: The d-pawn recaptured on c6, so nothing defends e5. The queen could go to d4 to attack the knight, but taking on e4 would lose the queen to the rook on e1. The knight keeps the pawn; the engine confirms a gain of a pawn.

items.prompt: Same position, but White's rook stands on f1 instead of e1. Does 1.Nxe5 win a pawn?

claims.statement: Nxe5 does not win a pawn along the engine's line.
No white piece defends e4.

hints: Look at what defends the pawn on e4.
After Nxe5 the black queen can go to d4 and then take on e4.
No: Black wins the pawn back.
items.explain: Without the rook on e1, e4 has no defender. After Nxe5 Black can simply take on e4 with the knight, or play Qd4 and, after Nf3, Qxe4: the queen takes the pawn back with no check. The engine rates the position level, so the pawn is only borrowed.

items.prompt: Same as the first position, but Black's h-pawn stands on h6. Does 1.Nxe5 win a pawn?

claims.statement: Nxe5 still wins at least a pawn.
No black piece defends e5.

hints: The pawn on h6 is on the other wing.
The defenders of e5 and e4 have not changed.
Yes: the h-pawn does not matter.
items.explain: The pawn on h6 does not touch e5 or e4, so nothing changes: no black piece defends e5, and the rook still guards e4. The move that matters is the rook on e1, not the h-pawn.

items.prompt: The bishop has retreated to b3. Tap every square it attacks (squares holding its own pieces count).

claims.statement: The bishop on b3 attacks exactly these squares.

hints: The bishop moves along diagonals and stops at the first piece.
Four directions: two toward the queenside, two toward the centre and kingside.
Include a2 and c2 (own pawns) and f7 (the first black piece on that diagonal); d1 is hidden behind c2.
items.explain: The bishop on b3 looks along two diagonals. Toward the kingside it passes c4, d5 and e6 and stops at the black pawn on f7. Toward the queenside it reaches a4. On the other side it touches its own pawns on a2 and c2; the diagonal stops at c2, so d1 is not attacked.

items.prompt: White to move, rook on e1. Black's pawn is still on b7 and the knight stands on c6. Does the bishop on a4 attack the knight?

claims.statement: One white piece attacks c6.

hints: Look at the diagonal from a4 to c6.
Is there a piece on b5?
Yes: b5 is empty, so the bishop sees c6.
items.explain: The bishop on a4 looks along the diagonal a4, b5, c6. With b5 empty it attacks the knight on c6 directly.

items.prompt: Same position, but Black's pawn stands on b5 instead of b7 (...b5 has been played and attacks the bishop). Does the bishop on a4 still attack the knight on c6?

claims.statement: No white piece attacks c6.

hints: Look at the diagonal from a4 to c6 again.
Which square on it is now occupied?
No: the pawn on b5 blocks the diagonal.
items.explain: The new pawn on b5 stands between the bishop and the knight, so the bishop no longer attacks c6. In this opening the pawn push both attacks the bishop and ends the pressure on the knight.

items.prompt: Same as the first position, but Black has also played ...h6. Does the bishop on a4 attack the knight on c6?

claims.statement: One white piece attacks c6.

hints: Is the h6 pawn on the diagonal a4 to c6?
Nothing on b5 has changed.
Yes: ...h6 does not matter.
items.explain: The pawn on h6 is far from the diagonal from a4 to c6, so the bishop still attacks the knight.

items.prompt: White to move on move 8. The bishop stands on b3 and the pawn on e4 is defended by the rook. Find a sound move.

claims.statement: 8.c3 and 8.a4 are each within 40 cp of the engine's top choice (depth 16).
8.d4 scores at least 50 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).
8.Nxe5 scores at least 300 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: White would like to play d4, but something is missing for the pawn on d4.
A pawn on c3 supports d4; a pawn on a4 asks a question on the other wing.
Play c3 (or a4).
items.explain: The pawn on c3 supports d4 and frees c2 for the bishop. Playing d4 at once loses a pawn to ...Nxd4 and, if the queen retakes, a bishop to ...c5 and ...c4. Grabbing on e5 loses a knight for a pawn. The engine accepts c3 and a4.

feedback_by_move.d2d4: Black takes on d4 and the queen cannot retake safely: ...c5 and ...c4 trap the bishop.
feedback_by_move.f3e5: dxe5 and the knight is lost for a pawn.

items.prompt: Black to move on move 8. White has just played c3. Find a sound move.

claims.statement: 8...O-O, 8...Bg4 and 8...Be6 are each within 40 cp of the engine's top choice (depth 16).
8...Nxe4 scores at least 300 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).
8...d5 scores at least 80 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Black's king is still in the centre, and White has a pawn on e4 that is guarded.
Castle, or develop the bishop on c8.
Play O-O (...Bg4 and ...Be6 also work).
items.explain: Castling takes the king to safety. The bishop on g4 or e6 develops the last minor piece, which is also sound. Taking on e4 loses a knight for a pawn because the rook on e1 recaptures, and ...d5 opens the centre too early.

feedback_by_move.f6e4: Rxe4: the rook recaptures and Black has lost a knight for a pawn.
feedback_by_move.d6d5: exd5 Nxd5 and White gets a strong centre with d4.

items.prompt: Black to move after 10.d4. The pawn on e5 is attacked twice and defended once. Find a sound move; one of the good ones adds a defender.

claims.statement: 10...Nbd7 and 10...Bb7 are each within 40 cp of the engine's top choice (depth 16).
After Nbd7 two black pieces defend e5.
10...exd4 scores at least 30 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Which Black piece can reach a square from which it sees e5?
The knight on b8 can go to d7.
Play Nbd7 (...Bb7 also works, by hitting e4).
items.explain: The knight on d7 sees e5 and joins the pawn on d6 as a second defender, so dxe5 dxe5 Nxe5 would not win a pawn. The engine also accepts Bb7: it hits e4, so after dxe5 dxe5 Nxe5 Black has play against that pawn. Taking on d4 is a little worse, because cxd4 gives White the centre.

feedback_by_move.e5d4: cxd4 and White's pawns on d4 and e4 control the centre; Black has no compensation.

items.prompt: White to move on move 6. Black has played ...b5 at once and the bishop on a4 is attacked. What do you play?

claims.statement: 6.Bb3 is within 40 cp of the engine's top choice (depth 16).
6.Bxb5 scores at least 300 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Which retreat keeps the bishop?
Only one square is both safe and useful.
Bb3.
items.explain: The bishop has two moves, b3 and the capture on b5. The capture loses a piece for a pawn (axb5), so the bishop retreats to b3, where it aims at f7. The same retreat works whether or not the rook has reached e1.

feedback_by_move.a4b5: axb5 and White has lost a bishop for a pawn.

items.prompt: Black to move. White has just played Re1. What do you play?

claims.statement: 6...b5 and 6...d6 are each within 40 cp of the engine's top choice (depth 16).
6...O-O scores at least 50 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).
6...Nxe4 scores at least 300 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Two natural moves lose material or a pawn here.
The bishop on a4 and the rook on e1 together create a threat against e5.
b5 or d6.
items.explain: The pawn on d6 defends e5 and the pawn on b5 attacks the bishop and ends the pressure on c6. Castling at once allows Bxc6 and Nxe5 winning a pawn; taking on e4 loses a knight for a pawn to the rook.

feedback_by_move.e8g8: Bxc6 dxc6 Nxe5 wins a pawn: the rook on e1 stops the queen from taking on e4.
feedback_by_move.f6e4: Rxe4: the rook recaptures, and Black has lost a knight for a pawn.

items.prompt: White to move on move 10. Black has just played ...Na5, which attacks the bishop on b3. Find a sound move.

claims.statement: 10.Bc2 is within 40 cp of the engine's top choice (depth 16).
10.d4 scores at least 40 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: The bishop on b3 is attacked by the knight. Which square can it retreat to?
An earlier pawn move emptied a square next to the bishop.
Bc2.
items.explain: The pawn move c3 left c2 empty, so the bishop retreats there and still defends e4. Pushing d4 at once ignores the attack on the bishop, and the engine rates it about three-quarters of a pawn worse.

items.prompt: White to move. Black has just retreated the knight to b8. What is White's plan?

claims.statement: 10.d4, 10.a4, 10.Bc2 and 10.d3 are each within 40 cp of the engine's top choice (depth 16).

hints: The pawn on c3 was played for a reason.
A pawn push in the centre uses it.
items.explain: White's pawn on c3 supports d4, and the move that uses it is the main line. The quiet moves a4, Bc2 and d3 are also within 40 cp, so the engine allows several plans.

items.prompt: Black to move after 9.h3 Bb7 10.d4. Find a sound move.

claims.statement: 10...Re8 and 10...Nb8 are each within 40 cp of the engine's top choice (depth 16).
10...Nxe4 scores at least 100 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Look at who attacks e5 and who defends it.
The pawn on d4 and the knight on f3 attack e5; the pawn on d6 and the knight on c6 defend it.
Re8 or Nb8 hold; taking on e4 loses a piece.
items.explain: The pawn on d4 and the knight on f3 attack e5, and the pawn on d6 and the knight on c6 defend it: two against two, so there is no threat yet. The rook on e8 adds support and the knight on b8 prepares Nbd7. Taking on e4 loses a knight for a pawn, because the rook on e1 recaptures.

feedback_by_move.f6e4: Rxe4 and Black has lost a knight for a pawn.

items.prompt: Black to move after 5.O-O. Find a sound move.

claims.statement: 5...Be7, 5...Nxe4 and 5...b5 are each within 40 cp of the engine's top choice (depth 16).
5...d5 scores at least 100 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: The pawn on e4 is loose, and the king on e8 is not yet safe.
Develop, or take the pawn the next lesson recommends, or gain space.
Be7 (Nxe4 and b5 also work).
items.explain: The bishop on e7 prepares castling, the capture on e4 is playable (the Open Defence, next lesson), and ...b5 kicks the bishop. A pawn push to d5 walks into Nxe5, because the knight on c6 is the only defender of e5.

feedback_by_move.d7d5: Nxe5 and White wins a pawn.
